Subject: Post-demo recap + sandbox eval plan (next tests vs cloud inference APIs)

Hi Oliver — great meeting earlier today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can get the sandbox lined up and the competitive tests scoped: 

Recap (very short)
- You showed the internal triage flow and the outputs you'd expect from the LLM (clinical summarization + structured coding suggestions).
- Main concerns: hallucination safeguards, per-token cost at 99th percentile latency SLAs, data controls (PHI), and vendor comparison against Vertex/Azure.

Requested next steps (my proposal)
1) Sandbox environment by Nov 9: provide sample payloads (anonymized) and we’ll run end-to-end inference plus the regression prompt set.
2) Competitive baseline: run identical prompt set on Redwood-hosted model variants and on two cloud inference APIs (Vertex AI - text-bison style and Azure OpenAI - gpt-4o/azure equivalent). Report: latency distribution (p50/p95/p99), per-token cost estimate, and hallucination rates.
3) Model-quality focus: hallucination definition we’ll use (false-fact rate + unsupported-assertion score), instruction-following score, and entity extraction F1 where applicable.
4) Security/compliance ask: we’ll also attach SOC2 evidence and a short checklist for VPC/private deployment questions.

Attachments: demo-recording.mp4 (link below), mvp-eval-checklist.xlsx (simple matrix you can fill with sample IDs)

Proposed owner roles:
- Redwood: Marcus (plan & run evals), Marissa (product config & differentiators), Tessa (solutions + onboarding).
- Acme: Oliver (technical lead), Natalie (procurement/legal contact).

Can you confirm: 
- Nov 9 works for the sandbox start?
- Responsible person for uploading the anonymized sample payloads to the Drive link?

Thanks — I’ll schedule the kickoff once you confirm.

Best,
Sean

Sean — thanks for the concise summary and the recording. Nov 9 for sandbox start is reasonable. A few clarifications before we lock dates: 

1) For the competitive baseline can you confirm which exact model families you’ll run on Redwood? We want a like-for-like (cost/perf) comparison — e.g., Redwood quantized-7B, 13B, and a larger 70B family if feasible.
2) For the cloud APIs we will ask our infra to run the same prompt set on Vertex and Azure. Could you provide the prompt runner (scripts) or a reproducible harness?
3) Hallucination metric — we like your false-fact rate approach. Please add a short example of the labeling rubric so our SME can pre-label a small set.
4) Compliance: we will need SOC 2 Type II evidence and a named MSA contact for procurement.

I’ll add Natalie Chen (procurement) on follow up — natalie.chen@acmehealth.com. For sandbox data upload we’ll have our data engineer (external) drop anonymized JSONL into the Drive link by EOD Nov 6.

If Redwood can deliver the evaluation harness and a short rubric by EOD Nov 4, we’re good to proceed. Otherwise push start to Nov 11.

Oliver

Oliver, Sean — putting a concrete eval plan below so expectations are aligned. I’ve attached eval-plan.md (markdown stub) with the runnable commands. High level: 

Eval matrix (short)
- Models: Redwood-quant-7B, Redwood-13B, Redwood-70B-quant, Vertex-text-bison-equivalent, Azure-gpt-4o-equivalent (note: cloud costs vary by tokenization).
- Workloads: clinical-summary (long-form), code-suggestion (structured), instruction-following prompts (multi-turn), hallucination stress-set (adversarial).
- Metrics: latency (p50/p95/p99), tokens-per-second, estimated $/1000 tokens, hallucination-rate (labelled), instruction-following accuracy (binary per prompt), entity-extraction F1.

Hallucination rubric (short)
- Label "Supported": the model output contains only facts supported by the provided inputs or widely-known facts.
- Label "Unsupported": the output asserts facts not derivable from inputs or that are contradicted by source material.
- Hallucination-rate = (#Unsupported) / (total labelled outputs).

Regression checks
- We’ll run pre-specified prompt list of ~120 prompts used internally to validate if any regression on instruction-following or hallucination occurs when switching kernel/quant configs.

Repro harness
- I’ll drop a small runner (python) into the shared Drive with instructions for calling Vertex/Azure and Redwood endpoints; includes tokenization normalization and cost estimators.

Timeline (tight)
- Nov 4 EOD: Redwood provides harness + rubric (I’ll own).
- Nov 6 EOD: Acme uploads anonymized sample JSONL.
- Nov 9–10: Redwood runs baseline across variants and cloud APIs and returns initial summary.
- Nov 12: short sync to review results and next optimization steps (quantization/batching).

Attachments: eval-plan.md (includes command examples and metric calculators).

Notes: For cost comparisons we’ll normalize to per-1M tokens and include an estimated infra overhead (network and cold-start penalties) for the cloud endpoints. If Acme prefers we can also run a throughput-backed test with VMs pinned to a single region to measure tail latency.

Happy to adjust — will send the harness link after this thread.

— Marcus

Oliver — adding a couple product/differentiator notes so they’re baked into the plan: 

- Cache & batching: we’ll enable prefix caching and our KV-cache during Redwood runs to show real-world cost reductions for repeated clinical templates. Please confirm if you want the cache disabled for a pure model-only comparison.
- Canary/rollout: once we have a preferred variant, Redwood can run a canary with traffic-split on the sandbox app and show live regression monitoring (alerts on instruction-following drop/hallucinations).
- PHI handling: we propose a simple PII redaction step as part of the ingest pipeline — we can provide a redaction pattern and a small script to run locally before upload.

If Acme’s legal needs a named MSA contact: please loop in procurement — Sean, I can be the product contact but legal/commercial routing should go to our contracts team (contracts@redwood.ai).
